content:
alex: Quick share — ran a lightweight profile on the p99 regression from yesterday. Seeing two hotspots: kernel selection churn on long-context requests and sporadic KV cache miss spikes that line up with batching backpressure. Posting raw notes and a small ask: can we add a per-route 'pipeline slice' card to Console showing token-level breakdown + KV hit/miss rates so PMs can correlate regressions to model/prompt patterns?

michelle: +1. we currently have route-level p50/p95 p99 and overall token latency but not split by token pipeline stage. Agree a slice makes it actionable.

rahul: For kernel churn — we log kernel_choice per inference in trace but it's not aggregated for routes. We can emit `kernel_variant` tag to metrics and add a count/latency histogram. cheap to add.

sara: KV behavior is interesting — I traced a user session where cache miss rate jumped from 8% to 28% after a config rollout (reduced prefix cache TTL). That matches the time of the regression. We should add `kv_prefix_hit_rate` and `kv_miss_latency` to the route card. Also want a separate time-series for `kv_eviction_count`.

liam: Batching heuristics: when the autoscaler pushes small batches to meet latency SLOs, we get more CPU context switching and occasional queueing. Suggest metric `batch_size_pXX` and `batch_fill_time_pXX` so we can see whether smaller batch fills correlate with higher per-token latency.

perf-bot: PERF ALERT: baseline vs latest commit shows +19% p99 token-latency on route `/chat/long-context` (investigate). Link: https://perf.internal/reports/2003/1234

alex: Thanks — action items I'll record: (1) emit kernel_variant histograms by route (rahul), (2) add kv_prefix_hit_rate, kv_miss_latency, kv_eviction_count (sara), (3) batch_size_p50/p95 and batch_fill_time metrics (liam), (4) Console card mock + example queries (michelle + me). Can we get quick sketches and queries by EOD?

michelle: sketch incoming. For Console card I'd propose these panes: top-line p50/p95/p99 tokens, middle waterfall of token stages (tokenize -> model -> kv lookup -> postproc) with stacked p95, bottom mini-timeseries: throughput (rps), error-rate, kv_hit_rate. Also add small control to toggle kernel_variant filter.

rahul: sample metric proto I propose to emit (promql-like):
```
# kernel variant breakdown by route
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(kernel_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/chat/long-context"}[5m])) by (le, kernel_variant))
# kv hit rate
sum(rate(kv_hits_total{route="/chat/long-context"}[5m])) / (sum(rate(kv_hits_total{route="/chat/long-context"}[5m])) + sum(rate(kv_misses_total{route="/chat/long-context"}[5m])))
```

sara: That looks good. For kv_miss_latency we'll also emit `kv_miss_latency_seconds` histogram to get p50/p95/p99. We should be careful about cardinality for `kernel_variant` values — limit to canonical variants (e.g., avx2, cuda-fastrun, quantized-8bit).

liam: One more thought: add a sampling flag so we only emit detailed token-stage breakdown for 1% of requests by route to avoid cost blowup. Console card can show sampled vs unsampled counts.

alex: Agree on sampling. For the UI we should show an annotation when sampling <100% so users understand it's sampled. Also include a quick drilldown modal that lists recent traces (link to trace UI) for the selected time window.

michelle: I'll mock the Console card in Figma and attach queries + wireframes here in thread. If folks can comment on metric names by lunchtime I'll align with telemetry schema.

rahul: I'll open a PR to add `kernel_variant` tag + histograms. Will include unit test and rollout flag. ETA tomorrow morning.

sara: I'll add KV metrics and a small benchmark to validate eviction counters. ETA EOD.

liam: I'll add batch metrics and an experiment to try 2 alternative fill time thresholds. We'll run on a subset of routes.

alex: Great. Final note — let's mark the route `/chat/long-context` as highest priority for the dashboard because it's where the regression surfaced. We'll sync in the perf sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: NOTE: linked benchmark run queued. /perf status will update when finished.
